Details and retained failures: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/2#issuecomment-6674259622. No new scientific acceptance, live attribution, commit/push, publication or external contact.

---

## Earlier checkpoints and original scope (retained)

## Previous D50 profile checkpoint — 2026-11-05

The investigator approves the first profile/result block. A detached owner profile and shared descriptor-delegation parameters are implemented in the isolated private dev8 source, with explicit unused/unknown/declared settings and no backend preparation or calculation. Final source/installed qualification remains pending after shared-host memory guards interrupt the build; this issue is not resolved merely by source delivery.

Details: https://github.com/uibcdf/hydramp/issues/2#issuecomment-6674259622; product owner #4, consumer uibcdf/peptidemt#32. Preserve accepted resources, native definitions and all earlier proposal evidence below.

## Original proposal (preserved)

PeptideMT needs a provider-owned, machine-readable description of the selected HydrAMP generation/descriptor profile so result provenance can identify its definitions without maintaining a second editable parameter table in the consumer.

Consumer: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8
This is a separate nonblocking metadata-capability proposal from numerical-drift investigation #1.

Source inspected: the local, unpublished native PyTorch port, `hydramp-torch==0.0.0.dev3`, wheel SHA-256 `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`. Its `hydramp_torch/properties.py` SHA-256 is `c47bd6f8224b996b6d221caf2de151d3d6aae1360faf4a3ec56fdd8b09abe758`. This is artifact/source evidence, not a claim that the port is committed or publicly distributed.

Observed gap: `Modlamp433Properties` exposes `expected_version` and `pi_amide`, but other selected parameters live in method bodies: Eisenberg scale, moment window 1000/angle 100/modality=max, charge pH 7/amide=True, and the selected pI amide=False. The generation branch also defines unfiltered AMP mode, one attempt, original-zero-token scoring, returned AMP order and raw AMP/MIC meanings. There is no complete supported data-only profile record tying those meanings to the implementation. The earlier consumer qualification helper described these values itself; extending that pattern to the public adapter would duplicate provider knowledge.

Proposed capability, for owner review: publish a versioned pure-data record or public metadata operation owned by HydrAMP that describes the selected implementation, supported native route, descriptor parameters/defaults, native score meanings and relevant source/version identity. Reading it should require no checkpoint/PCA loading or descriptor/model evaluation; a packaged data resource is one possible delivery, with the implementation choice left to the provider. Clearly distinguish descriptive method defaults from evidence of a peptide's actual chemistry or scientific acceptance.

Suggested acceptance evidence:
- values correspond to the actual delegated descriptor/generation calls;
- callers cannot accidentally mutate a shared profile;
- resource/operation works without real model/PCA assets;
- unsupported or different profiles are explicit;
- preserve native calculations, scores, chemistry assumptions and existing qualification evidence.

Current consumer interim behavior: retain exact installed-provider Python hashes, implementation/version/descriptor class identity and source references; user documentation explains the selected definitions. Do not introduce another computational implementation or pretend the metadata is unavailable scientific evidence. When the provider record is delivered and its exact candidate is qualified, PeptideMT can consume it and remove any interim consumer-authored profile description.

This proposal does **not** request changing scientific definitions, precision, weights or descriptors, executing new models, publishing a package, or silently adopting a new candidate. The current dev3 bundle and proposed single installed-adapter qualification remain unchanged.

## Original proposal (preserved)

PeptideMT needs a provider-owned, machine-readable description of the selected HydrAMP generation/descriptor profile so result provenance can identify its definitions without maintaining a second editable parameter table in the consumer.

Consumer: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/8
This is a separate nonblocking metadata-capability proposal from numerical-drift investigation #1.

Source inspected: the local, unpublished native PyTorch port, `hydramp-torch==0.0.0.dev3`, wheel SHA-256 `81761e0d48d92f0956e0afc28b3b4154f16032de53c666fd2cfbb53606102ed7`. Its `hydramp_torch/properties.py` SHA-256 is `c47bd6f8224b996b6d221caf2de151d3d6aae1360faf4a3ec56fdd8b09abe758`. This is artifact/source evidence, not a claim that the port is committed or publicly distributed.

Observed gap: `Modlamp433Properties` exposes `expected_version` and `pi_amide`, but other selected parameters live in method bodies: Eisenberg scale, moment window 1000/angle 100/modality=max, charge pH 7/amide=True, and the selected pI amide=False. The generation branch also defines unfiltered AMP mode, one attempt, original-zero-token scoring, returned AMP order and raw AMP/MIC meanings. There is no complete supported data-only profile record tying those meanings to the implementation. The earlier consumer qualification helper described these values itself; extending that pattern to the public adapter would duplicate provider knowledge.

Proposed capability, for owner review: publish a versioned pure-data record or public metadata operation owned by HydrAMP that describes the selected implementation, supported native route, descriptor parameters/defaults, native score meanings and relevant source/version identity. Reading it should require no checkpoint/PCA loading or descriptor/model evaluation; a packaged data resource is one possible delivery, with the implementation choice left to the provider. Clearly distinguish descriptive method defaults from evidence of a peptide's actual chemistry or scientific acceptance.

Suggested acceptance evidence:
- values correspond to the actual delegated descriptor/generation calls;
- callers cannot accidentally mutate a shared profile;
- resource/operation works without real model/PCA assets;
- unsupported or different profiles are explicit;
- preserve native calculations, scores, chemistry assumptions and existing qualification evidence.

Current consumer interim behavior: retain exact installed-provider Python hashes, implementation/version/descriptor class identity and source references; user documentation explains the selected definitions. Do not introduce another computational implementation or pretend the metadata is unavailable scientific evidence. When the provider record is delivered and its exact candidate is qualified, PeptideMT can consume it and remove any interim consumer-authored profile description.

This proposal does **not** request changing scientific definitions, precision, weights or descriptors, executing new models, publishing a package, or silently adopting a new candidate. The current dev3 bundle and proposed single installed-adapter qualification remain unchanged.
